narration.text: Why galaxies drift toward one hidden region of space.
Astronomers call it the Great Attractor.
It lies about 150 to 250 million light-years away.
Galaxy motions there differ by up to 700 kilometres per second.
Our own galaxy's dust hides it from ordinary telescopes.
Infrared and radio surveys had to peer through.
So even galaxies get tugged by unseen neighbours.
